summary_md: **Cryptography and Security Papers ([@FSFG](https://x.com/FSFG/status/2116431213598593388))** shares *REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents* by Ren, Tak and Wang ([arXiv 2610.39155](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39155)), which models required assets as a dependency graph to enforce least privilege against prompt injection while separating discovery from authorization.

referenced_urls.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents

media.description: Abstract of the REALM paper on identifying minimal required assets for least-privilege agents.
media.ocr_text: Large language model (LLM) agents often receive access to more files, accounts, and services than a task requires. Prompt injection turns this excess access into an opportunity to redirect execution toward unrelated resources. Applying least privilege therefore requires identifying the assets needed by a task, including assets whose identities emerge only during execution. We present REALM (Required Execution Assets Linked to a Mission), an approach to identifying and maintaining a task's required assets and their permitted uses. The approach represents required assets as Dependency Graph nodes, resolves prerequisite relationships, and admits newly discovered assets through source-scoped selection.
